title: Sidecar narration push stalls unsubmitted in orch pane on pane-not-idle fallback
description: When pane %0 is not idle at send-keys time, sendKeysVerified's idle-gate times out and the sendOnceUnverified fallback dumps the text into the orchestrator's input WITHOUT an effective Enter, so the [cam] narration line sits unsubmitted until the operator manually presses Enter. Observed live 2026-07-23 on the plan-escalated push for CAM-398: the operator had to intervene or the loop would have sat idle forever. This is a live recurrence of the CAM-375/CAM-364/CAM-404 UNDELIVERED send-once class. The fallback should either retry until the pane goes idle instead of dumping unverified text, or guarantee submission; a stalled narration breaks the autonomous loop because the orchestrator never observes the terminal.

spec.scope: Guarantee that a sidecar narration push actually SUBMITS in the orchestrator pane, on both send paths. IMPORTANT, the hypothesis filed in this issue's own description is measurably WRONG and must not be implemented: both send paths already emit `tmux -L cam send-keys -t <pane> <text> Enter` as a single call with Enter as a separate argv element and with no `-l` (src/tmux/dispatch.ts:602-606 on the idle path, src/tmux/dispatch.ts:474-478 in sendOnceUnverified). Nothing is missing the Enter key. The measured defect is that NEITHER path remediates a non-submission. On the idle path (dispatch.ts:553-640) the payload is sent exactly once at :602-606 and the loop at :609-635 retries only the VERIFICATION, never any submission, so a genuinely dropped Enter (capture-pane lags one refresh cycle behind a busy Ink TUI, acknowledged at dispatch.ts:22-25) produces one `push-undelivered` event and the line sits in the composer forever. On the pane-not-idle path, waitForIdlePane times out against a 2 s narration budget (NARRATION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, dispatch.ts:278, wired at src/supervisor/host.ts:344, roughly ten 200 ms probes) and sendOnceUnverified fires a single send with zero geometry sampling, zero verification and zero retry, so delivery is unknown by construction. This explains both live occurrences: the second one had a provably idle pane, which means it went down the VERIFIED path, which also cannot remediate. The fix is to make submission, rather than text delivery, the property that is guaranteed: run the existing verify loop on BOTH paths, and when verification fails, remediate by sending a BARE submit key with no text argument, then re-verify. A bare submit key is duplication-safe and does not violate the CAM-375 send-once guard, because that guard forbids re-sending the payload TEXT, not pressing Enter: if the text landed, Enter submits it; if the text never landed, Enter submits an empty composer, which is a harmless no-op. Also unify the two paths so the pane-not-idle fallback stops being blind, and split the event taxonomy so a push recovered by remediation is distinguishable from a first-try success and from a terminal failure. Out of scope: changing NARRATION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS (CAM-361 chose 2 s deliberately so a busy pane cannot stall the loop for 30 s), touching the Dashboard.tsx or worker-report.ts send paths, and any composer-clearing or bracketed-paste work.
acceptanceCriteria: sendKeysVerified performs the payload send exactly once on BOTH the idle path and the pane-not-idle fallback path, and the post-send verify loop now runs on the pane-not-idle path too (it no longer returns blind immediately after an unverified send). [oracle: bun test test/dispatch.test.ts]

When post-send verification fails, the remediation sends a BARE submit key (tmux send-keys -t <pane> Enter, with no text argument) and then re-verifies; the payload TEXT is never re-sent on any path, preserving the CAM-375 send-once guard. [oracle: bun test test/dispatch.test.ts]

A real-tmux integration test (real tmux server on an isolated socket, real pane, not argv-shape assertions against a fake) proves end to end that a payload delivered while the pane is not idle sits unsubmitted, and that the bare submit key subsequently submits it. [oracle: bun test test/integration/dispatch-geometry.test.ts]

The push event taxonomy distinguishes recovery from terminal failure: a push that succeeded only after at least one bare-submit remediation emits a distinct event kind from both a first-try success and a terminal failure, and push-undelivered remains reserved for the terminal case. [oracle: bun test test/unit/dispatch-orch-pane-busy.test.ts]
The narration idle budget is unchanged in value and the fix does not lengthen how long the sidecar blocks waiting for the pane to go idle. [oracle: bun test test/tmux/dispatch-timeouts.test.ts]
The full quality spine is green. [oracle: bun run check:all]

The dispatch module header records the corrected diagnosis, replacing the issue's filed hypothesis: both send paths already include Enter and neither uses -l, so the defect is unremediated non-submission, not a missing submit key. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
gotchas: Do NOT implement the hypothesis in the issue description. Grounded and measured 2026-07-24: sendOnceUnverified (src/tmux/dispatch.ts:463-481) DOES include Enter as a separate argv element and does NOT use -l. There is no missing submit key to add.

Never add `-l` to any send-keys call. `-l` makes ALL args literal, so the trailing `Enter` argv element becomes the literal text `Enter` instead of a submit. This exact bug shipped once (CAM-55) and is guarded by the real-tmux test at test/integration/sendkeys-submit.test.ts:38-70.

The CAM-375 send-once guard (documented in the header at src/tmux/dispatch.ts:71-81, tested at test/dispatch.test.ts:430 and test/integration/dispatch-geometry.test.ts:107 and :170) is a hard invariant: the payload TEXT is physically sent at most once per push. Re-sending the text produced the triple-delivery symptom recorded in scripts/cam/journal.md:136 and :147. A bare submit key carries no payload and therefore does not breach this guard, but any implementation that re-sends `text` does and must be rejected.

The verification oracle is cursor geometry, not content: sampleCursorGeometry (src/tmux/display-message.ts:106-127) runs `tmux -L cam display-message -p -t <pane> '#{cursor_x};#{cursor_y};#{pane_width};#{pane_height}'` and fails CLOSED, returning null on non-zero exit, blank or unparsable output; a null on either side counts as not-delivered (dispatch.ts:614). Delivery is inferred from geometryUnchanged (dispatch.ts:343-345) AND cursorRowStartsWithPrompt (dispatch.ts:397-402). Preserve the fail-closed semantics.

There are TWO distinct capture readers and the decoupling is deliberate: `capture` (injected, feeds the idle gate) versus `visibleCapture` (always built fresh from tmuxSpawnFn, feeds the prompt-row discriminator) at dispatch.ts:574-585. The supervisor path passes a FULL-SCROLLBACK reader (src/supervisor/host.ts:588-595) while the sidecar paths pass a VISIBLE-SCREEN reader (host.ts:271-276). Do not collapse them.

isOrchPaneIdle (dispatch.ts:317-325) is a pure capture-pane content match with an END-anchored IDLE_PROMPT regex, and the module's own measurement at dispatch.ts:355-359 records that the real claude composer row reads `❯ Try "how do I log an error?"` and therefore provably does NOT match that end anchor. Do not assume the idle gate is reliable; that is exactly why the fallback path needs verification rather than a longer wait.

Do NOT lengthen the wait as the issue suggests ("retry until the pane goes idle"). NARRATION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS is 2 s by deliberate design (CAM-361, dispatch.ts:278) so a busy pane cannot stall the sidecar loop for 30 s. The remediation must make the SEND verifiable, not the WAIT longer.

Back-to-back send-keys race the orchestrator Ink prompt; merge-watch.ts:658-661 coalesces to exactly one notifyOrchestrator call on the success path specifically because of this. Keep the SEND_KEYS_SETTLE_MS (50 ms, dispatch.ts:242) settle window before any verify or remediation rather than firing keys immediately.

The real-tmux integration tests are all `test.skipIf(!tmuxAvailable)` and drive isolated private sockets (`cam-it-dispatch-geometry`) with a `cat` or `test/fixtures/dispatch-geometry/raw-echo.ts` receiver, never a real claude TUI. Follow that pattern; do not attempt to boot a claude session in a test.
No foreground `sleep` in tests or scripts (harness-blocked) and macOS has no `timeout` binary. Poll async waits with `waitForCondition`, never a fixed setTimeout.

Both send calls use `{ stdio: 'ignore' }` and discard the spawn return, so a non-zero tmux exit (dead pane, wrong target) is today indistinguishable from success on both paths (dispatch.ts:602-606, :474-478). If the remediation checks the submit-key spawn status, keep that change scoped and do not silently alter the payload-send behavior.

sendOnceUnverified is module-private with exactly one caller (dispatch.ts:589). sendKeysVerified has two callers (src/supervisor/host.ts:338-345 for narration, and the sendKeysWhenIdle proxy at dispatch.ts:649-651 used by src/commands/issue.ts:195, src/commands/spec.ts:228 and src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts:431). A change to the shared verify loop affects all of them; keep the 30 s default idle budget for the CLI callers intact.
This is sidecar-executed and orch-facing code, so the shipped binary and the running sidecar both need a coherence rebuild afterwards; note it but do not perform it from inside a story.
domainTerms: idle gate: the pre-send waitForIdlePane poll loop (dispatch.ts:422-439) that blocks until isOrchPaneIdle matches or the idleTimeoutMs budget expires.
send-once guard: the CAM-375 invariant that the payload text is physically send-keys'd at most once per push, with retries re-verifying rather than re-sending.
submit remediation: the new bounded action of sending a bare Enter with no text argument, in order to submit a payload already sitting in the composer.
geometry oracle: the cursor_x/cursor_y equality check (geometryUnchanged) used to infer that the composer emptied.
prompt-row discriminator: cursorRowStartsWithPrompt, the second half of the delivery inference, requiring the row at cursor_y to start with a prompt glyph.
push-undelivered: the worker event emitted on terminal non-delivery, carrying a reason of pane-not-idle or retries-exhausted.
